- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk premium or mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model underreacts to mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses tail risk or policy-driven corrections; if sentiment shows policy uncertainty (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33), add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment is trending upward but price is flat or declining, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–2 days; if sentiment turns bullish, forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead, not delayed.
